bio:
Hello and welcome to my portfolio !

My name is Théo 'Phenomene' Hentgen. 30 years old and currently living in France.

My past experiences in China, Europe, Asia and North America have led me to work in four different languages and work with different cultures.

I have a degree in Sports with Physical, Mental, and Psychological courses. I also have a master in Esports Communication.

I have been playing football (or soccer, if you're from North America) for 20 years. I have been the captain of all my teams and this is where I started to build a strong leadership and develop my will to become a coach.

I have now been a Siege coach for 6 years, you'll find all my past experiences in said category.

Do not hesitate to contact me if you want to know more or if you have any questions !

items.title: TEAM GOALS TOOL
items.text:
• Weekly planning
• Setting up collective goals
• Improvements focused on the week ahead

items.title: PLAYER IMPROVEMENT TOOL - PART 1
items.text:
• Weekly or bi-weekly review, done with the player
• Setting up individual goals and points of improvement
• We go through the period together: what worked, what did not, and why
• The player fills his own part, so the review stays a conversation and not a verdict

items.title: PLAYER IMPROVEMENT TOOL - PART 2
items.text:
• Review of the week, one sheet per session: date, opponent, map(s)
• Positives first, then the learning areas - what the player took away from the week: about himself, about the game, about the team
• Out of those, one MAIN learning area, so he leaves with a single priority instead of a list
• Main focus for the next session written twice: what the coach sees, and what the player himself wants to work on
• Best rounds and learning rounds noted, so the review is watched and not just talked about
• Confidence level filled by the player (low / medium / high) twice per meeting: once at the start, once at the end - the gap between the two tells me what the review actually did for him, and how to handle him in the days after
• Kept between reviews and checked again at the next one, so progress is tracked over the season instead of restarting every month

items.title: MENTAL WORK & STRESS MANAGEMENT - PART 1
items.text:
• Imagery points filled by players
• Review with the coach during individual meetings
• Following up imagery exercises (Internal or external)
• Every day and before matches
• Imagery helps a lot in anticipating highly stressful situations
• Makes your decision faster and better on gameday
• Increases your focus and calm

items.title: MENTAL WORK & STRESS MANAGEMENT - PART 2
items.text:
• Feedback filled by players after official games
• Review with the coach
• Debrief to help the player improve on his mental/stress management

items.title: MENTAL WORK & STRESS MANAGEMENT - PART 3
items.text:
• Breathing exercises before practice and matches - a player who knows how to control his breath stays calmer under pressure, and comes down from a high-pressure situation faster
• Activation exercises before scrims and officials - 5 to 10 minutes of reflex and focus work to switch the brain and the muscles on, so nobody starts flat. It also builds a routine, and the routine itself reduces stress
• Positive thoughts worked on day to day, in individual and team meetings - players are held accountable for negative thought patterns, because a confident team is part of a healthy system
• A coach has to catch negative behaviour early and address it right away rather than let it settle
• Imagery kept running every day and before matches, on top of the exercises above
• I analyse the team's and each player's needs to plan how much of those exercises they actually need - some have to calm down, others have to switch on - and I adjust the volume through the season depending on the schedule and the pressure of the event

items.title: BANK - BASEMENT SPLIT - ATK
items.text:
• Called when the enemy roams

• Players take their positions, drone their own area and count: everyone calls what they see and what they do NOT see (enemies, utility, traps)

• REACTIONS - from those calls we pick the entry where the enemy is weakest in numbers and/or utility, so we always play a man advantage (2v1, 3v1, 3v2)

• Site hit: if one player is blue stairs alone, or alone on site

• Top clear: if there is a strong Hori roam with traps

• Mid hit Archives: if nobody is archives, or one player with little trap coverage

• Mid hit Open: same read as Archives, but in Open

items.title: BANK - CEO DEFAULTS - ATK
items.text:
• Three default ways to attack Top

• Open trump windows

• KILL - focus the Trump player, kill him and keep flooding. If Ace/Hibana are banned, take an execute operator (Ying/Grim/Sens)

• PLANT - create chaos with Sens/Rauora. Once Sens pulls the wall, Rauora jumps in through the door to plant while Glaz pushes jani door to deny a C4 or a smoke on the plant. Ace/Hibana clears stock hallway, or Flores/Ying if banned. Flash Soda and push, Dokkaebi backstab or spiderman

• STOCK OPENING KILL - cheese play for the opening kill on the stock player: when he falls back because the wall is open, or Capitao fires him, rappel upside down on main skylight to kill him

items.title: CHALET - MASTER/OFFICE - ATK
items.text:
• Rush K9

• Once Sens pulls up the wall covering master area: Osa destroys K9 barricade and BB push, killing the guy half wall

• Dokkaebi flashes piano to cover K9 entrance and holds it from the boost or jump in Ivy window

• Ying flash sol & master, then rappels in to create chaos

• During all of that, Osa plants on the door behind her shield

• Sens puts claymores on lobby door and trench

items.title: BORDER - BATHROOM/TELLERS - DEF
items.text:
• 60% winrate DEF

• Horizontal strat on Bathroom site

• The top setup and Valkyrie reinforcing hatches late in prep phase to make the enemy think we play top to force them clearing it

• Hide Kaid and use it for hatches to keep them closed

• Valkyrie/Mozzie play top early to shoot drones and make enemy lose time then fallback and play horizontal

• Play the c4 kills with info we have

• Late round, If enemy does an East take and courtyard execute into tellers we can deny that with C4/smokes if they didnt work vertical properly and hatch not open

• We can also have a line of sight from custom and retake Passport/Top

items.title: BANK - OPEN AREA/STAFF - DEF
items.text:
• 75% winrate DEF

• Top setup for Open area

• We close meeting wall to janitor to create a stronger hold top and have good crossfires between Trump/Elevator & Meeting, which throws off a lot of teams

• Like the strat says, we play to die

• If enemy wants to clear it, Valkyrie can flank lobby or square and Azami can come up marble stairs

• If enemy goes directly for the square, Azami can delay with her Kibas & Goyo canisters

• Meanwhile, Joker (means that player can play everything) and Castle can come back help holding archives and site

• Goyo can pressure top square or come closer to site

items.title: KAFE - READING - ATK / TRAIN TARGET
items.text:
• Counter built from their own VODs: in one of their Reading defences, Kaid was isolated in Train - alone, no gadget to help him, no Dining rotate and no line of sight to support him

• So we explode mining window with Blitz/Buck/Sens to kill him there, Ying holding his chimney fall back, Rauora controlling the top flank with her gadget

• Once he is down we flip and flood Reading: Sens stays Train to bait the Dining plant, Blitz/Buck push Reading door, Ying flashes cocktail + laundry through the drone hole, Rauora peeks new hatch

• Called only once we ID Kaid - they do not run him on any of their other defences

• Every phase of the take is drawn on its own blueprint, with the operator line-up above the strat

items.title: KAFE - KITCHEN - ATK / HORI RUSH
items.text:
• Rush designed against their roam setup on Kitchen

• I noticed that with Tub/Kaid they close Bakery and Freezer and roam heavy top, leaving only the Tub on site in Freezer and absolutely no trap on the reception side

• So we push fast reception into site, into Freezer, and kill the Tub before the roamers can come back

• Then plant and hold the rotations: red side, VIP/Bar side and the hatch drop

• One blueprint with every player's path and entry point, so the rush stays coordinated instead of being a coin flip

items.title: KAFE - MINING - DEF / FAKE AGGRO
items.text:
• M80 knew both of our Mining defences: the fall out into Kitchen to deny the plant with Pulse/Valk, and the aggressive one where we fight for top floor control

• So I wanted to make them think we were running the aggressive strat

• We show the fight and hold top floor for a minute or more, then fall back into Kitchen and play to deny the plant

• Valkyrie hides during prep phase and three C4s are lined up for the plant deny

• A counter-strat in the real sense: they prepared against our habits, so the strat is built on what they expect to see

items.title: OPPONENT ANALYSIS & GAME PLAN - LAIR
items.text:
• Two slides per map: the opponent analysis first, then the game plan

• ANALYSIS - their attack and defence bans, our own, and the bans we expect them to use against us

• Attack and defence notes broken down per bombsite, built from their recent games - the source matches are referenced so every read stays traceable

• A summary that boils the detail down to two usable lines for the players: how they attack, how they defend

• GAME PLAN / DEFENCE - the defence plan per bombsite, with the player adjustments that go with it

• GAME PLAN / ATTACK - built to help the IGL guide the team and call the right attack depending on the triggers they see in the round

• Each call carries its operator swaps per player, plus the fallback if a key operator gets banned

items.title: OPPONENT ANALYSIS - OTHER FORMATS
items.text:
• Same preparation, delivered in whichever format the team and the staff actually read

• Annotated blueprints: their start, their anchors and the reads we expect, written straight on the map

• Setup boards next to it, so players see the positions instead of reading about them

• Highlighted notes for the moments that decide the round, kept short enough to be remembered in game

• I adapt the format to the structure and to the players - slides, blueprints, boards or written notes - rather than forcing one template on everyone
